themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints spiked to 13 this week, up 236% from the 3.9-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, signaling a sudden emergence of neighborhood friction over sidewalk seating and street use in Greenwich Village/SoHo.
evidence: 13 outdoor dining complaints this week vs. 3.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.8)
236% spike represents statistically significant deviation from 8-week baseline
Issue emerged suddenly this week, not a long-running pattern
reporting_angles: Interview residents and restaurant owners about specific outdoor seating conflicts (noise, obstruction, quality of life)
Investigate whether this reflects post-holiday surge in dining activity or new enforcement by Community Board/311 awareness

themes_detail.label: Root and Sewer Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Root/sewer/sidewalk condition complaints exploded to 4 last week, up 3100% from the 0.1 weekly average, indicating a potential citywide or neighborhood-specific underground infrastructure failure requiring immediate investigation.
evidence: 4 complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 11.72, highest severity spike in data)
3100% increase represents most dramatic statistical anomaly in district
Aligns with community board recurring budget request for DEP catch basin cleaning
reporting_angles: Contact DEP to identify specific locations affected and investigate whether freeze-thaw cycles or aging infrastructure are responsible
Map complaints geographically to determine if problem is concentrated in older neighborhoods (SoHo) or citywide

themes_detail.label: Curb Damage and Degradation
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints jumped to 13 last week, a 550% spike from the 2.0 weekly average, suggesting accelerated pavement deterioration or vehicle damage concentrated in this high-traffic district.
evidence: 13 complaints last week vs. 2.0 weekly average (z-score: 11.0, severity: high)
Converges with sidewalk condition spike (19 complaints, +158%) suggesting broader street infrastructure problem
reporting_angles: Investigate whether winter weather, heavy commercial vehicle traffic, or for-hire vehicles (Uber/Lyft) are causing accelerated curb damage
Compare curb repair response times and budget allocation to this district vs. others

themes_detail.label: Asbestos Detection Spike
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints surged to 3 last week, a 1100% increase from the 0.2 weekly average, likely indicating reports during renovation or demolition activities in this dense residential-commercial district with older buildings.
evidence: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.35, severity: high)
1100% spike coincides with high DOB alteration filing volume (1,426 alterations in 90 days)
Greenwich Village/SoHo contains many pre-1970s buildings with asbestos-containing materials
reporting_angles: Cross-reference asbestos complaints with specific DOB permit locations to identify which renovation projects may lack proper asbestos abatement protocols
Investigate whether contractors are properly disclosing and managing asbestos during alterations; contact NYC DOH for compliance enforcement data

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Vehicles Accumulation
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned vehicle complaints rose to 9 last week, up 260% from the 2.5 weekly average, suggesting either increased vehicle dumping in this congested district or heightened resident awareness and 311 reporting.
evidence: 9 complaints last week vs. 2.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.33)
Aligns with community board recurring request for additional sanitation trucks and equipment
reporting_angles: Determine average NYPD/Sanitation response time for abandoned vehicle removal and whether capacity is strained
Interview parking enforcement and sanitation officials about whether this reflects seasonal dumping or systemic removal delays
